newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may sell UES stake as convertible bond.
newsitem.headline: Russia may sell UES stake as convertible bond.

text.p: Russia may wait until the end of the year to sell a government-held stake of about 1.5 percent of national electric company UES, possibly as convertible bonds, a senior privatisation official said on Tuesday.
"There are quite a few suggestions on that question, whether to sell shares or issue convertible bonds, Russian Federal Property Fund first deputy chairman Vladimir Malin told Reuters.
"UES is the easiest of all to sell off, and we know that the share (price) is going up, so we might wait until the end of the year."
The Russian government owns 52.7 percent stake of UES. The government has said it will sell 1.5-2.0 percent of UES but maintain a controlling 51 percent stake.
UES shares, which traded at about eight cents in early December, were $0.3170 at 0930 GMT on Tuesday on the Russian Trading System after $0.3198 at the close on Monday.
